critical.issue: Revenue resolves to fee income ($6.57B Q1'26) instead of total net revenue ($21.45B Q1'26). Root cause: in /app/backend/market.py:192-194, `_FIN_CONCEPTS['revenue']` lists `us-gaap_RevenueFromContractWithCustomerExcludingAssessedTax` at index 1 and `us-gaap_RevenuesNetOfInterestExpense` at index 4. `_pick()` returns the first non-null match. WFC reports BOTH tags, so fee income wins. Fix: move `us-gaap_RevenuesNetOfInterestExpense` to the FRONT of the list (any filer that reports it is a bank/insurer and that tag IS their total revenue; non-bank filers don't report it, so order is safe). JPM/BAC/GS pass because they don't report RevenueFromContractWithCustomerExcludingAssessedTax at the quarterly level, so RevenuesNetOfInterestExpense wins by default.

critical_code_review_comments: market.py _pick() uses first-match semantics on a priority list. For a mixed universe of banks + non-banks, bank-specific XBRL tags MUST be listed BEFORE generic tags, otherwise a bank that happens to also report a generic tag (fee income under RevenueFromContract…) will mis-resolve.

The composite fallback `revenue = InterestIncomeExpenseNet + NoninterestIncome` is sound and would also give WFC the correct ~$22B value — but it only runs when `_pick` returns None, and `_pick` returned a (wrong) non-null value for WFC, so the fallback never executed.
No `-m` filter or test discovery issue; both backend test files share conftest.py cleanly.

rca_of_issue: WFC revenue mis-mapping RCA: Finnhub returns WFC's quarterly 10-Q filings with multiple revenue-like concepts. For Q1 FY26 (YTD, end 2026-03-31): us-gaap_RevenueFromContractWithCustomerExcludingAssessedTax=$6,577M (labelled 'Fee income') AND us-gaap_RevenuesNetOfInterestExpense=$21,446M (labelled 'Total revenue'). market.py _FIN_CONCEPTS['revenue'] lists [Revenues, RevenueFromContract…ExcludingAssessedTax, SalesRevenueNet, RevenueFromContract…IncludingAssessedTax, RevenuesNetOfInterestExpense]. _pick() iterates in order and returns the first non-null, so for WFC it picks fee income $6,577M instead of total revenue $21,446M. The subtraction logic then produces quarterly fee-income-only values ($3.7B–$6.9B) and inflated net_margin_pct (>100%). Reproduction: python /tmp/wfc_api.py (prints Q3 FY24 rev=$3.78B with nm=135.3%). Mitigation: reorder the list so RevenuesNetOfInterestExpense is checked first — zero risk to non-bank tickers because they don't report that tag. JPM/BAC/GS escape this bug only because they don't report the fee-income tag at the quarterly level and so the generic entries all miss, falling through to the bank tag.
